chapter: Carnegie Hall and the touring years
title: The first blues concert at Carnegie Hall
summary: John Hammond's Carnegie Hall blues show with Big Bill (who took off his tight shoes), Pete Johnson, Ammons and Lewis.

blocks.x: During World War Number Two. And, uh, we were runnin' back and forth to New York an' all over the country. Gettin' back to New York, I was uh...forgot to tell you that the first blues show that ever was at Carnegie Hall, John Hammond gave it, an' I was on the show. Had Big Bill from Chicago, a host of other blues singers... Big Bill had on some tight shoes were hurtin' his feet. He would stand up on the stage playin' and cryin'.
So John Hammond asked him what was he cryin' about. He said, "These shoes kill me."
So John Hammond say, "Well, take 'em off."
So he took his shoes off and done the show. Barefoot!
That was your first trip to New York. You came to New York to do that concert, didn't you?
John Hammond brought you there for that concert. Had you heard all these other people before that were on that concert?
I'd heard of Big Bill out of Chicago but he about the only one I heard. Pete Johnson was there...Albert Ammons...Meade Lux Lewis. Was really a jam-up show.
